correctness.rationale: The affine difference map on three parabola points is invertible for p>=5. A pair of distinct zeros yields pairwise distinct pth-root phases, and its rank-two cofactor kernel fixes all three magnitude ratios as triangle chords. If a cyclic gap exceeds p/2, its chord ratio is >sqrt(2), while balanced gaps have ratio <sqrt(2) for p>=7. All gaps shorter than p/2 admit strict integer smoothing unless they are balanced. The p=5 partitions are exhausted separately. Every gap pattern is realizable on every support by the difference map. The unit-circle line-section bound limits any three-sparse sum to two zeros, justifying counting 6 or 12 displacements per first zero and dividing ordered pairs by two. An independent standard-library script checked 62,664 finite candidate chord ratios and 2,478 constructed-null/grid checks across 23 prime orders; these tests do not replace the analytic proof.

originality.rationale: The new mathematical invariant is the sharp minimum max/min coefficient magnitude necessary for TWO zero frequency samples of an arbitrary complex three-atom prime-parabola Fourier signal, with complete minimizing ratio-phase geometry and an exact count of minimizing projective coefficient rays. Li and the closely related full published three-sparse spectrum establish the maximum zero count (two) but neither imposes nor optimizes amplitude dynamic range. The previously existing phase-only parabola result proves one-zero isolation and its near-zero frequency modulus: it explicitly excludes unequal amplitudes and hence does not imply this threshold. The published near-equilateral Riesz-conditioning classification optimizes eigenvalue ratios of a distinct 3x3 Fourier Vandermonde system, not amplitudes in the two-zero nullspace; its geometric balanced-gap fact is credited and not claimed alone. No stronger covering statement was found in the cited scoped and general searches.
residual_risks: An earlier unindexed polygon chord-spread theorem may give the same standalone geometric minimax; the novelty here is the complete parabolic two-zero amplitude threshold and equality ray enumeration.
No independent historical-priority or mathematical audit has been performed.

value.rationale: The precise coefficient dynamic-range threshold is natural for sparse Fourier interference and null-design: it measures the minimal unequal weighting needed to create a second exact frequency erasure once equal-magnitude signals cannot. The result is uniform over all three-element parabola supports and infinitely many prime dimensions, and classifies every sharp root geometry and counts all minimizing complex rays. It resolves a quantitatively motivated boundary absent from existing zero-count and phase-only results, not a merely chosen small finite table or an arbitrary substitute invariant.
